display.title: Episode 296: The King Is Watching (Erev Sukkos)
display.summary_short: The eve of Erev Sukkos: why everyone can help build the sukkah, how a guest is its finest decoration, and the story of a rabbi who taught a hungry coachman that the King is always watching.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the day before Erev Sukkos 5748. Uncle Yossi explains that unlike writing a mezuzah or making tefillin, which only experts may do, everyone young and old can help build and decorate the sukkah, and the most beautiful decoration of all is a guest who has no sukkah of his own. After the Hakochainik march comes an invitation to Tzivos Hashem's Sukkos Experience fair, and a yeshiva student leads the Shema. Story time follows the Yomim Noraim with a lesson in honesty: old Rabbi Yitzchak, traveling through a forest, gives all his food to his hungry coachman, who then wants to help himself to apples from the king's orchard. The rabbi agrees to keep watch, and just as the coachman reaches the top of the fence he calls out, 'He's watching!' Later he explains that he meant the King of all kings. The show ends with reminders to eat in the sukkah, invite guests, and bless the four kinds.
display.lesson: Hashem is always watching, so be honest and never take what is not yours; and beautify the sukkah by inviting guests.
